name: Chemosh
title: The national god of Moab
summary: Chemosh was the national idol of the Moabites, a foreign deity worshipped in defiance of the God of Israel. Solomon built a high place for Chemosh near Jerusalem, an act condemned as a grave sin. Chemosh is mentioned in several biblical contexts as a symbol of idolatry and apostasy from the true God.

keyEvents.title: The god of Moab mentioned in connection with Israel's wilderness journey
keyEvents.description: Chemosh is named as the god of Moab in relation to Israel's victory over Sihon, king of the Amorites, who had taken land from Moab. The Song of Heshbon mentions Chemosh's people as defeated.

keyEvents.title: Jephthah mentions Chemosh in negotiations with the Ammonites
keyEvents.description: Jephthah argued before the king of the Ammonites by referring to Chemosh as the god whom the Ammonites/Moabites believed had given them territory, just as the Lord had given Israel land.

keyEvents.title: Solomon builds a high place for Chemosh
keyEvents.description: King Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the detestable god of the Moabites, on the hill east of Jerusalem to please his foreign wives. This was regarded as a serious sin.

keyEvents.title: King Josiah's reforms remove the worship of Chemosh
keyEvents.description: During King Josiah's religious reforms, the high place that Solomon had built for Chemosh on the Mount of Corruption was destroyed and desecrated as part of a comprehensive cleansing of idolatry.

keyEvents.title: Jeremiah prophesies judgment against Chemosh and Moab
keyEvents.description: The prophet Jeremiah proclaimed God's judgment on Moab and declared that Chemosh would go into captivity along with his priests and princes, as a sign of Moab's downfall.
